newsitem.title: USA: U.S. agency to seek change in Heathrow flights - NYT.
newsitem.headline: U.S. agency to seek change in Heathrow flights - NYT.

text.p: The General Accounting Office is expected to testify in favour of American Airlines and British Airways Plc giving up a number of their landing rights at London's Heathrow Airport, the New York Times said.
In Wednesday's edition, the Times said the GAO's stance is the first formal opinion from a federal agency on the proposed alliance between American, which is a unit of AMR Corp, and British Airways.

GAO officials are expected to testify before the Senate Commerce Committee later today that in order to foster greater competition, other U.S. airlines should be allowed to fly at least 23 daily round trips into Heathrow.
American and British Airways now account for 38, or 69 percent, of the 55 daily round trips between the U.S. and Heathrow.
American and British Airways declined to comment on the GAO's expected testimony.
